title: Бессонная ночь и приход хозяйки  (A Sleepless Night and the Owner's Arrival)

segments.t: Before the staff meeting in the lobby, Katya apologizes to Denis and says she could not sleep all night, while Denis hides the reason he barely slept—until owner Eleonora Andreevna walks in. Listen to the scene.
Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Hi, Denis.' Katya directs that line without fuss: opening with the casual greeting "privet" ("hi") signals right away that Katya and Denis are on familiar terms.
'Hi, Katya.' Denis puts this update plainly here: opening with the casual greeting "privet" ("hi") signals right away that Denis and Katya are on familiar terms.
'You were upset because of yesterday.' Katya responds briskly to settle things, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'No, everything is fine.' Denis frames one key touch in earnest: "normalno" means "fine, OK", and it carries the main weight of what Denis is saying.
'Forgive me, please.' Katya delivers that remark calmly now: dropping in "pozhaluysta" ("please") keeps the request polite on the surface even in a brisk exchange.
'I was very worried all night.' Katya follows up bluntly in their talk, without trying to dress up how she really feels.
'I did not sleep at all today.' Katya frames one pointed piece at once: "segodnya" means "today", and it carries the main weight of what Katya is saying.
Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
'I did not sleep all night either.' Denis opens up evenly facing Katya, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'I tossed and turned all night long.' Denis jumps in candidly with Eleonora, making his position completely clear.
'It is clear why you did not get enough sleep.' Katya uses this direct expression in earnest: "vyspalsya" means "got enough sleep" (from "vyspatsya"), giving the line its exact edge.
О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
'Report any problems to me immediately.' Eleonora cuts in calmly as things stand, shifting the whole mood of the room in a single beat.
А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
'And here is the owner of our hotel.' Eleonora continues lightly in this moment, without trying to dress up how she really feels.
'I did not come here to get acquainted.' Eleonora leans on one familiar detail at once: "znakomitsya" means "get acquainted", and it carries the main weight of what Eleonora is saying.
Я тоже всю ночь не спал.
О любых проблемах сразу сообщать мне.
А вот и владелица нашего отеля.
And that introduces hotel owner Eleonora Andreevna. See you next time!
